title.description: Subject line, shaped like '11-05 Brief · <the one thing that matters most today>'. Under 60 characters. Always English, whatever language the entries are in.

lede.description: One or two sentences in English: what in today's batch is actually worth the reader's time. An empty string when nothing is.

sections.description: Grouped by subject, the group that matters most first. A group holding one entry is still a group.

heading.description: Your own name for the group, in the language its entries share -- English when they do not share one. Never copy a feed's channel title.

title.description: The entry's title, in the language its source wrote in. When several sources cover one event, this is one entry whose title names the event itself.

summary.description: Two to four sentences in the language the source wrote in -- never a translation: what happened, and why it is worth reading. Never restate the title, never open with 'This article discusses'.

links.description: Links to the sources. A merged entry lists every one of them, each under a label that distinguishes it from the others.

label.description: What is at the other end of this link, and it must be distinct from every other label in the same entry. The outlet's name alone ('FT', 'HN discussion', a blog's name) when that already tells them apart; when one outlet supplied several of the merged articles, name each one's own angle instead ('FT: the export-curb timeline', 'FT: Beijing's response'). A row of identical labels tells the reader nothing.

dropped.description: Entries judged not worth reading, by their original titles. Shown collapsed, so the reader can see your taste and correct it.
